subsystems.name: Heat transport loop
subsystems.role: collects waste heat from reactors, furnaces, smelters and habitats and carries it to the radiators.

subsystems.name: Temperature-lift stage
subsystems.role: radiators shrink as the fourth power of temperature, so heat pumps may be worth their own power cost.

subsystems.name: Solid-surface radiators
subsystems.role: the conventional option: panels that emit infrared to space.

subsystems.name: Droplet radiator
subsystems.role: sprays a sheet of droplets into the vacuum, exposing an enormous emitting area per kilogram, then recaptures them.

subsystems.name: Working fluid and materials
subsystems.role: the fluid sets the temperature range; the panel sets the mass per watt rejected.
parts: ammonia or HFE for moderate temperatures
liquid metals such as NaK or lithium for high temperatures

subsystems.name: Assembly and protection
subsystems.role: kilometre-scale panels must be stowed, deployed or built in orbit, and survive debris.
parts: isolation valves to bypass punctured panels

buildSteps.title: Fix the rejection temperature
buildSteps.detail: Start from a Stefan-Boltzmann calculation: at 300 K an ideal surface radiates about 460 W per square metre, roughly 0.9 kW/m² for a two-sided panel. One gigawatt therefore needs on the order of a square kilometre, so every degree of extra temperature is fought for.

buildSteps.title: Choose the loop architecture
buildSteps.detail: Single-phase liquid, two-phase (boiling and condensing), or liquid-metal. Two-phase loops move more heat per kilogram of pump; liquid metals carry heat out of very hot processes but demand careful materials compatibility.

buildSteps.title: Decide whether to pump the heat up
buildSteps.detail: Running a heat pump raises the radiator temperature and can cut its area several-fold, at the cost of extra electrical power. For a gigawatt plant this trade is the central design decision.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the panels
buildSteps.detail: Coolant channels are formed in a composite or metal face sheet, bonded to a stiff backing, then coated with a high-emissivity finish so most of the infrared actually leaves.

buildSteps.title: Stow and deploy
buildSteps.detail: Panels are folded, rolled or segmented so they fit inside a launch fairing, then unfolded and latched by hinges and robot arms once in orbit.

buildSteps.title: Or build a droplet radiator instead
buildSteps.detail: A generator sprays a thin sheet of droplets that radiate directly to space, and a collector — magnetic for liquid metals, electrostatic for insulating fluids — gathers them back into the loop, so the structure carries almost none of the mass.

buildSteps.title: Connect, fill and leak-check
buildSteps.detail: The loop is evacuated, charged with coolant, and tested for leaks, with isolation valves so one punctured panel does not drain the whole system.

buildSteps.title: Operate and protect
buildSteps.detail: Freeze protection, dust and micrometeoroid damage, and slow degradation of the emissive coating set how much capacity must be held in reserve.

prerequisites.tech: Large deployable and robotically assembled structures
prerequisites.why: orbiting stations have been assembled by robot arms, but nothing at the scale of a square-kilometre radiator array.
ammonia two-phase loops fly routinely on space stations; liquid-metal loops at megawatt scale remain laboratory and design work.
emissivity degrades under ultraviolet and atomic oxygen exposure, and the panels cannot easily be repainted.

prerequisites.tech: Orbital power sources of comparable size
prerequisites.why: a gigawatt of waste heat implies a gigawatt of process power, and no such orbital power or industrial plant exists.
the concept has been studied and bench-tested, but the droplet generator and collector have never run in orbit.

pathway.milestone: station-class active thermal control rejecting tens to hundreds of kilowatts through ammonia panels
pathway.unlocks: crewed orbital laboratories and instruments that need steady cooling.

pathway.milestone: megawatt-class radiators assembled or deployed robotically in orbit
pathway.unlocks: orbital smelting, fuel depots and larger habitats.

pathway.milestone: first flight test of a droplet radiator and of high-temperature liquid-metal loops
pathway.unlocks: a step change in kilograms per kilowatt rejected, which is what unlocks tens of megawatts.

pathway.milestone: gigawatt-scale heat rejection built from in-space materials
pathway.unlocks: the orbital industrial economy this tile is really about — until then, radiator area, not energy supply, is the ceiling.
